tagline: Rolling farmland links an Ogeechee River village with Warrenton’s courthouse square.
intro: Eleven miles of State Route 16 carry the Warren County-Piedmont Scenic Byway Extension over gently rolling hills, past farmland, rivers and a wildlife management area. Georgia DOT includes it among the state’s designated scenic byways, highlighting historic properties and the National Register districts of Jewell and Warrenton.

The corridor’s history reaches beyond this short drive: the route was part of the Native American Okfuskee Trail, which connected what is now Augusta with the Mississippi River. The scenic extension continues the Historic Piedmont Scenic Byway from Putnam and Hancock counties into Warren County.

Start at the Hancock-Warren county line beside Jewell, where the Ogeechee River marks Warren County’s western border. Jewell’s historic district lies on the Hancock County side of the river. Follow State Route 16 to Warrenton, ending at State Route 12 in the county seat.

moments.title: Jewell
moments.text: Jewell stands beside the Ogeechee River, where the water marks the western boundary of Warren County. Its other names include Jewells Mills and Rock Factory. Across the river in Hancock County, the Jewell Historic District encompasses a mill village. The district entered the National Register in 1979, with 37 contributing buildings and four contributing sites. Its architecture includes Late Victorian, Queen Anne and Gothic Revival styles.

moments.title: Beall Springs
moments.text: Beall Springs takes its name from the Beall family, the original owners of the town site. It is an unincorporated community in Warren County.

moments.title: Warrenton
moments.text: Warrenton’s red brick courthouse occupies a small square, with an octagonal dome and cupola above its hipped roof. The town became Warren County’s seat in 1797, four years after the county was established. Incorporation followed in 1810 as a town and in 1908 as a city. The courthouse dates from 1909, rather than Warrenton’s founding, and its Classical Revival design entered the National Register in 1980.
moments.notice: Above the red brick courthouse, an octagonal dome supports a cupola.
